text:
B: Hiya! Can you hear me alright? Sorry, that noise is Duke, the dog. He's snoring. If you hear something like a tractor, that's him.
A: Yes, I hear you. Hello.
B: I'm Ryan. I'm in Long Eaton, sort of between Derby and Nottingham. I teach history, Head of Year 9. Still got the lanyard on, look, I've not even got changed.
A: Tomasz. Peterborough. I am electrician in a food factory, team leader for engineering on shifts.
B: Oh nice, proper job that. What, keeping all the lines running?
A: Yes. Conveyors, motors, everything. New line keeps tripping out. They bring the installer, he doesn't know. I find the fault myself in one hour. Was earth leakage, cable damaged in the tray. And production manager asks every ten minutes "when is it fixed", like this helps.
B: Ha! That's SLT all over. "Can you just quickly..." Do you know what I mean?
A: SLT?
B: Sorry, senior leadership. Managers, basically.
A: Ah. Same everywhere.
B: I noticed in your photo there's a crucifix on the wall. Do you go to church at all?
A: Why you ask this?
B: Sorry, no, I wasn't being nosy. I just go myself, St Laurence's in Long Eaton. Sorry, ignore me.
A: Is okay. I am Polish, so Catholic. Christmas, Easter, and when my wife says. More culture than, you know.
B: Yeah, no, I get that.
A: You go every week?
B: Once a month, maybe. More when things are hard. It got me through when my dad died, to be honest. Sorry, that's a bit heavy for three minutes.
A: Is fine. You watch football?
B: Oh, don't. Derby County, my whole life. My dad took me, and now I share a season ticket with my cousin. We lost again Saturday, absolutely shocking, I were mardy all Sunday. Hannah, my wife, won't let me talk about it at tea anymore.
A: Derby. This is Championship, no?
B: Ha, that's harsh! Fair, but harsh.
A: My team is Lech Poznań. Also suffering. So I understand.
B: Also suffering. That's going on a T-shirt. Have you got kids?
A: Two. Daughter seventeen, doing A-levels. She wants driving lessons now, thirty-five pound an hour. Is a rip-off. I can teach her in car park.
B: Ha, my dad tried that with me in the Asda car park. Never again. We both came home not speaking.
A: My son is twenty, at Trent, in Nottingham.
B: Oh, Nottingham, that's my patch! I did my PGCE at the uni, and the school's just on the west side. What's he studying?
A: Engineering. Mechanical. He will be proper engineer, with a degree, not like—
B: Oh, that's brilliant, you must be dead proud of him, my mum still tells people I went to—
